title: The Riemann Hypothesis: Past, Present and a Letter Through Time
why: Connes' major survey of RH history plus new spectral/operator perspective from a leading researcher.

title: Prolate spheroidal operator and Zeta
why: Connes-Moscovici uncover new spectral property of prolate spheroidal operator tied to zeta.

title: Spectral Triples and Zeta-Cycles
why: Connes-Consani exhibit eigenvalues of Weil explicit-formula quadratic form via zeta-cycles.

title: Heat Expansion and Zeta
why: Connes computes full heat-kernel trace expansion for the conjectural RH self-adjoint operator.

title: Knots, primes and class field theory
why: Connes-Consani extend adelic/class field theory framework underlying spectral realization of L-function zeros.

title: Hilbert spaces and low-lying zeros of L-functions
authors: Emanuel Carneiro; Andrés Chirre; Micah B. Milinovich
why: Carneiro-Chirre-Milinovich unify Fourier optimization for low-lying zero density, rigorous analytic number theory.

title: On the Ruelle-Mayer Transfer Operators for Hölder Continuous Functions
why: Baumgartner extends Ruelle-Mayer transfer operator spectral theory linked to Maass forms and zeta zeros.

title: On the Berry-Keating Operator
why: Careful review clarifying rigorous status of the Berry-Keating operator's connection to RH.

title: High-Precision Approximation of Riemann Zeros via the Truncated Weil Form
why: Numerical study testing convergence of Connes-van Suijlekom truncated Weil form zeros to Riemann zeros.

title: Twisted moments of characteristic polynomials of random matrices in the unitary group
why: Baluyot–Conrey give a rigorous random matrix analogue of the Keating–Conrey moment recipe, a major structural advance.

title: Moments of zeta and correlations of divisor-sums: stratification and Vandermonde integrals
why: Introduces Vandermonde/Rodgers–Soundararajan-style integral expression underpinning the moment conjectures program.

title: Exchangeable arrays and integrable systems for characteristic polynomials of random matrices
authors: Theodoros Assiotis; Mustafa Alper Gunes; Jonathan P. Keating; Fei Wei
why: Fully settles moments of derivatives/real characteristic polynomials via exchangeable arrays, resolving a 25-year problem.

title: Negative moments of the Riemann zeta-function
why: Bui–Florea establish negative moments of zeta, a genuinely new and technically hard direction under RH.

title: Sharp bounds for joint moments of the Riemann zeta function
why: Curran–Heycock extend sharp joint moment bounds unconditionally across the full conjectured range, key benchmark result.

title: A survey of moment bounds for $ζ(s)$: from Heath Brown's work to the present
why: Florea's survey synthesizes Heath-Brown's legacy and the current moment-bounds landscape, valuable field overview.

title: Lower bounds for the large deviations and moments of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line
why: Arguin–Creighton give unconditional large-deviation/moment lower bounds on the critical line advancing the log-correlated program.

title: Amplified moments of the Riemann zeta function
why: Amplified moments yield unconditional sixth-moment lower bounds matching Keating–Snaith predictions, a strong new advance.

title: Currently there are no reasons to doubt the Riemann Hypothesis: The zeta function beyond the realm of computation
why: Farmer's widely-discussed rebuttal of RH-doubting arguments, blending RMT evidence, shapes community consensus.

title: Bulk asymptotics of the Gaussian $β$-ensemble characteristic polynomial
why: Lambert–Paquette's rigorous bulk asymptotics of Gβε characteristic polynomials deepen the RMT-zeta analogy foundations.

title: The Fyodorov-Hiary-Keating Conjecture. II
authors: Louis-Pierre Arguin; Paul Bourgade; Maksym Radziwiłł
why: Completes the FHK conjecture lower bound, establishing tightness of zeta's maximum on short intervals—a landmark result in the field.

title: Maxima of a Random Model of the Riemann Zeta Function over Intervals of Varying Length
authors: Louis-Pierre Arguin; Guillaume Dubach; Lisa Hartung
why: Introduces the foundational random model interpolating log-correlated and IID extreme-value regimes, seeding much subsequent work.

title: The Fyodorov--Hiary--Keating Conjecture on Mesoscopic Intervals
why: Extends FHK-type sharp bounds to mesoscopic intervals, advancing the program beyond the original fixed-length regime.

title: Maxima of log-correlated fields: some recent developments
authors: E. C. Bailey; J. P. Keating
why: Authoritative survey synthesizing log-correlated field theory and its connections to zeta/L-function extreme values.

title: Large Deviation Estimates of Selberg's Central Limit Theorem and Applications
why: Sharp unconditional large-deviation bound for Selberg's CLT, improving Soundararajan/Harper and feeding into maximum estimates.

title: Freezing transition and moments of moments of the Riemann zeta function
why: Establishes the freezing transition for moments of moments of zeta, confirming Fyodorov-Keating predictions rigorously.

title: A model problem for multiplicative chaos in number theory
why: Soundararajan-Zaman model problem links random multiplicative functions to multiplicative chaos, clarifying the probabilistic mechanism behind FHK-type phenomena.

title: A dichotomy for extreme values of zeta and Dirichlet L-functions
authors: Andriy Bondarenko; Pranendu Darbar; Markus Valås Hagen; Winston Heap; Kristian Seip
why: Establishes a dichotomy linking Dedekind zeta large values to improved zeta maxima bounds, connecting distinct extreme-value programs.

title: Dirichlet $L$-functions on the critical line and multiplicative chaos
why: Proves convergence of random Dirichlet L-functions to Gaussian multiplicative chaos, extending the log-correlated framework beyond zeta itself.

title: On the Pólya Frequency Order of the de Bruijn Newman Kernel. Certified Failure at Order Five and the Toeplitz Threshold Phenomenon
why: Rigorous computational disproof that the de Bruijn–Newman kernel is PF5, refining structural understanding of the Λ constant program.

title: Note on the positivity of the real part of the log-derivative of the Riemann $ξ$-function near the critical line
why: Establishes explicit positivity bounds for the log-derivative of ξ near the critical line, refining zero-free region heuristics.

title: Equivalent criteria for the Riemann hypothesis for a general class of $L$-functions
why: Extends Riesz/Hardy-Littlewood-type equivalent criteria for RH to a general class of L-functions, broadening the positivity-criterion framework.

title: An explicit formula for the zeros of the Riemann zeta function
authors: Eugenio P Balanzario; Daniel Eduardo Cardenas Romero
why: Gives an explicit Hermite-weighted formula linking zeta zeros directly to primes, a genuine explicit-formula advance.

title: A smooth version of Landaus explicit formula
authors: Eugenio P. Balanzario; Daniel Eduardo Cardenas Romero; Richar Chacon Serna
why: Produces a smoothed Landau explicit formula and links zero-location resolution to prime detection via an uncertainty-principle argument.

title: A Prime Power Equation
why: Constructs an entire Fourier-transform function vanishing at zeta zeros, yielding a zero-free prime power ident

title: New large value estimates for Dirichlet polynomials
why: Guth–Maynard breakthrough large-value estimates for Dirichlet polynomials, major input to zero-density theory.

title: Half-isolated zeros and zero-density estimates
why: Maynard–Pratt introduce half-isolated zeros method improving classical Ingham–Huxley zero-density estimate.

title: New exponent pairs, zero density estimates, and zero additive energy estimates: a systematic approach
authors: Terence Tao; Tim Trudgian; Andrew Yang
why: Tao–Trudgian–Yang systematic exponent pairs and zero-density estimates via new ANTEDB database.

title: Explicit zero-free regions for the Riemann zeta-function
authors: Michael J. Mossinghoff; Timothy S. Trudgian; Andrew Yang
why: Mossinghoff–Trudgian–Yang give widely-cited explicit zero-free region improvements for zeta.

title: Zero-free regions inspired by work of Heath-Brown
authors: Chiara Bellotti; Tim Trudgian; Andrew Yang
why: Bellotti–Trudgian–Yang extend Heath-Brown's Linnik-constant ideas to sharpen explicit zero-free region.

title: Zeta Zeros on the Critical Line
authors: Daniel A. Goldston; Ade Irma Suriajaya
why: Goldston–Suriajaya survey fifty years of pair correlation method and its applications.

title: Fourier optimization and Montgomery's pair correlation conjecture
authors: Emanuel Carneiro; Micah B. Milinovich; Antonio Pedro Ramos
why: Carneiro–Milinovich–Ramos apply Fourier optimization framework to sharpen Montgomery's pair correlation bounds.

title: An unconditional Montgomery Theorem for Pair Correlation of Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function
authors: Siegfred Alan C. Baluyot; Daniel Alan Goldston; Ade Irma Suriajaya; Caroline L. Turnage-Butterbaugh
why: Baluyot–Goldston–Suriajaya–Turnage-Butterbaugh prove unconditional analogue of Montgomery's pair correlation theorem.

thread_name: General RH / critical line / large values
title: Pair Correlation of Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function I: Proportions of Simple Zeros and Critical Zeros
authors: Siegfred Alan C. Baluyot; Daniel Alan Goldston; Ade Irma Suriajaya; Caroline L. Turnage-Butterbaugh
why: Extends Montgomery's pair correlation method to new horizontal-distribution results on zeta zeros, by leading researchers in the area.

thread_name: General RH / critical line / large values
title: Zeta Zeros in a Narrow Vertical Box
authors: Daniel A. Goldston; Ade Irma Suriajaya
why: Companion advance replacing RH with an explicit double-sum estimate to control simple critical-line zeros.

thread_name: General RH / critical line / large values
title: Short mollifiers of the Riemann zeta-function
authors: J. Brian Conrey; David W. Farmer; Chung-Hang Kwan; Yongxiao Lin; Caroline L. Turnage-Butterbaugh
why: Conrey-Farmer et al. improve Levinson's method via calculus of variations, strengthening critical-line zero-proportion results.

thread_name: General RH / critical line / large values
title: Large value estimates in number theory, harmonic analysis, and computer science
why: Guth's survey unifies large value problems across analytic number theory, harmonic analysis, and CS, framing open directions.
